reading: The motif in one corner is completed to 4-fold symmetry about the grid centre; where a mirrored pair of cells on one row or column has a different-coloured cell two steps inward, that colour is repeated every second cell between the pair (dotted edge lines).

slots.motif: all input fg cells (one corner quadrant)
slots.axes: grid centre row, centre column and diagonals (D4 overlay)
slots.dotted_line: for two mirrored same-colour cells E on one row/column whose step-2 inward neighbour has colour D, every second cell strictly between them gets D

why: output = D4 overlay of input plus dotted lines; mirrored pairs without a step-2 neighbour (e.g. the 8s in pair 2) get no dots

reading: The partial pattern is completed so the grid is symmetric under flips and transpose (D4); fg cells are overlaid with their mirror images.
why: output equals the overlay of the input with its horizontal, vertical and diagonal mirror images (pair 1 needs the diagonal)

reading: The big colour-2 rectangle extends to the grid border in all four directions along each of its rows and columns, except lanes on a side that contain a marker cell; those lanes stay empty (markers kept).

new_rows.name: open_lanes
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(O) :- osize(O, N), N > 3.
inbig(Y, X) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
mk(Y, X) :- fgc(Y, X), !inbig(Y, X).
top(O, min(Y)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bot(O, max(Y)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
lft(O, min(X)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
rgt(O, max(X)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
incol(X) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
inrow(Y) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
upblk(X) :- mk(Y, X), big(O), top(O, A), Y < A.
dnblk(X) :- mk(Y, X), big(O), bot(O, B), Y > B.
lfblk(Y) :- mk(Y, X), big(O), lft(O, L), X < L.
rtblk(Y) :- mk(Y, X), big(O), rgt(O, R), X > R.
open_lanes(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), incol(X), !upblk(X), big(O), top(O, A), Y < A.
open_lanes(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), incol(X), !dnblk(X), big(O), bot(O, B), Y > B.
open_lanes(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), inrow(Y), !lfblk(Y), big(O), lft(O, L), X < L.
open_lanes(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), inrow(Y), !rtblk(Y), big(O), rgt(O, R), X > R.

why: every background cell in a block row/column lane outside the block becomes 2 unless a marker lies in that lane on that side
invariants: cells outside the block's row and column bands

reading: Where four 2-cell dominoes point at one background cell from left, right, above and below (each ending two cells away), that centre cell becomes 4.

new_rows.name: cross_centre
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, K).
cross_centre(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, K), !fgc(Y, X), A = Y - 2, B = Y - 3, fgc(A, X), fgc(B, X), D = Y + 2, E = Y + 3, fgc(D, X), fgc(E, X), F = X - 2, G = X - 3, fgc(Y, F), fgc(Y, G), H = X + 2, I = X + 3, fgc(Y, H), fgc(Y, I).

why: the only changed cells are background cells with fg at distance 2 and 3 in all four orthogonal directions; each becomes 4

reading: A line of 6s ends in a 2; a ray shot from the 2 away from the 6s crosses the 7 field and the first frame cell it hits turns 7.

new_rows.name: ray_hit
new_rows.datalog:
dir(DY, DX) :- cell(Y, X, 2), off(DY, DX), A = Y - DY, B = X - DX, cell(A, B, 6).
ray(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 2).
ray(A, B) :- ray(Y, X), dir(DY, DX), A = Y + DY, B = X + DX, px(A, B, 7).
ray_hit(A, B) :- ray(Y, X), dir(DY, DX), A = Y + DY, B = X + DX, cell(A, B, K).

why: exactly one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 (direction 2 minus adjacent 6), and it becomes 7 (7 is the background)

reading: Every 2 cell lying inside (or on the edge of) a green rectangle gets a 3x3 ring of 1 around it, the 2 kept in the centre; 2s outside rectangles are left alone.

new_rows.name: boxed_twos
new_rows.datalog:
c3(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, 3).
top(O, min(Y)) :- c3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bot(O, max(Y)) :- c3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
lft(O, min(X)) :- c3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
rgt(O, max(X)) :- c3(O), obj(O, Y, X).
boxed_twos(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 2), c3(O), top(O, A), bot(O, B), lft(O, L), rgt(O, R), A1 = A - 1, B1 = B + 1, L1 = L - 1, R1 = R + 1, Y > A1, Y < B1, X > L1, X < R1.

why: unit is the 3x3 block 111/121/111 centred on each anchor; overlapping copies keep the anchor 2s (adjacent anchors occur in pairs 1 and 2); rings may overwrite 0 and outside 2s
invariants: cells farther than 1 from any anchor

reading: The grid is a lattice of 4x4 boxes (period 5). An odd-coloured cell that appears at the same in-box position in two boxes of the same box-row or box-column is copied into that position of every box between them.

slots.lattice: boxes of 4x4 separated by background lines, period 5
slots.anomaly: an interior cell whose colour differs from the regular box pattern at that position (rare colour)
slots.pair: two anomalies of the same colour at the same in-box position in one box-row or box-column
slots.action: paint that colour at the same in-box position in every box strictly between the pair

why: changed cells are exactly the in-between positions of same-colour, same-position anomaly pairs along box rows/columns

reading: The bottom row and the right column carry runs of colours; each colour fills the rectangle whose columns are its run in the bottom row and whose rows are its run in the right column.

new_rows.name: run_cross
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, K).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, K).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, K).
run_cross(Y, X) :- maxy(M), maxx(N), cell(M, X, K), cell(Y, N, K), !fgc(Y, X).

why: background cell (Y,X) takes colour c exactly when the bottom-row cell in column X and the right-column cell in row Y both have colour c; colour is that shared c (per cell), not a constant

reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
why: output is a 1x2 tiling of the input in every pair

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k x k times, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.

slots.count: number of distinct colours in the input (2,2,4,3,3 in the pairs)
slots.layout: k by k grid of copies

why: output size is 3k x 3k with every block equal to the input; k matches distinct colour count, not pixel or object count
